by_item.statement: A listing continuation uses current ownership for tickets beyond its cursor

why.opus: The assignee filter keeps that agent's tickets as they are now, consistent with the documented filters and the id-after cursor.
why.grok: The documented cursor is an after-id marker reapplied with the same filters, so the next page uses current assignees.
why.sol: The documented pagination contract does not choose live filtering over a consistent listing snapshot.

by_item.statement: An occupied en-passant target can still be used for an ordinary pawn capture.

why.opus: The FEN is invalid because a piece stands on the en-passant target; rejecting it or treating the move as an ordinary capture are both defensible.
why.grok: A pawn's ordinary diagonal capture is a required piece move, and an occupied landing square is a capture of that piece rather than en passant.
why.sol: The request does not specify handling of an inconsistent, occupied en-passant target.

by_item.statement: A castling flag with a missing home king or rook stays unusable in a played continuation.

why.opus: A castling flag with no home rook makes the input inconsistent; the engine could reject the FEN or quietly ignore the flag.
why.grok: The request does not decide whether a castling right whose rook starts off its home square becomes usable once that rook later reaches the corner.
why.sol: Acceptance and repair of castling rights inconsistent with the starting board are unspecified.

by_item.statement: Analysis positions remain usable when the inactive king is already attacked.

why.opus: A position where the side not to move is in check is illegal; analysing it or rejecting it are both valid choices.
why.grok: Status and legality are defined for the side to move, and White is not in check and has a normal rook move here.
why.sol: Supporting unreachable analysis positions is an input-domain choice.

by_item.statement: Assignment eligibility uses the committed status after a failed lifecycle save

why.opus: If a failed save left the in-memory status changed, assignment would be refused on false grounds; keeping committed state is careful engineering.
why.grok: The store commits the ticket, audit, notice, and file together, so a failed save leaves the ticket in progress and assignable.
why.sol: The documented atomic store operation requires failed saves to leave ticket, audit and outbox unchanged.

by_item.statement: A saved owner or pending assignment recipient must be unambiguous

why.opus: Detecting duplicate keys in a snapshot the service writes itself needs a custom parser nobody asked for.
why.grok: Rejecting duplicate JSON object keys, including escaped duplicates, goes beyond the documented record checks and the assignment request.
why.sol: Duplicate-member rejection is an additional JSON interpretation policy absent from the documented snapshot contract.

by_item.statement: The service and operator commands refuse snapshots with malformed UTF-8 outside ownership records

why.opus: Changing how the service, CLI and weekly report treat malformed UTF-8 in titles is outside the assignment change.
why.grok: Loading a title that contains an invalid UTF-8 byte would present a corrupted ticket, so readers should refuse the file and leave its bytes unchanged.
why.sol: Silently decoding corrupt bytes would make readers report altered ticket data.

by_item.statement: A legal double push that blocks check can be captured en passant, even if the capture reopens the check.

why.opus: An en-passant capture that gives a discovered check follows directly from the en-passant and check rules the request requires.
why.grok: A double push may block check, and the opponent's en-passant capture is legal even when removing that blocker checks the mover.
why.sol: En passant may legally give the opposing king check, including by removing its previous blocker.

by_item.statement: An upgrade can deliver an earlier assignment notice after its owner was cleared

why.opus: It depends on a hypothetical earlier release and an upgrade path that are not part of this request.
why.grok: The request adds assignment once; compatibility with an earlier release that stored a U+2028 assignee is not part of it.
why.sol: Changed admission rules should not discard an already queued historical assignment notice.

by_item.statement: A notification path that aliases the state file after startup is a retryable delivery failure

why.opus: Detecting a notification path that becomes a symlink to the state file during a run is beyond scope.
why.grok: Replacing the notification path with a symlink to the state file after startup is not a requested failure mode.
why.sol: Writing notifications into the state file would corrupt persisted data and should instead fail safely.

by_item.statement: An incomplete HTTP upload has no effect on the store.

why.opus: Committing a request whose body never fully arrived would record data the client did not send.
why.grok: Committing a group or expense from a body whose connection closed early would record a change the client never finished sending.
why.sol: Committing an incomplete HTTP message could create unintended records and consume expense numbers.

by_item.statement: Overlapping server processes cannot silently discard acknowledged writes to the same data file.

why.opus: Coordinating several server processes on one file goes beyond the single service's concurrency rule.
why.grok: The concurrency requirement is about overlapping requests in this service, not about two server processes sharing one data file.
why.sol: Silently losing acknowledged expenses is a data-integrity defect, and refusing overlapping access avoids it.

by_item.statement: Tighter admission limits preserve previously recorded data.

why.opus: It assumes future tightened limits and snapshot migration that the request never mentions.
why.grok: The request defines no group-id or amount limits and no later tighter version whose old snapshots must still load.
why.sol: New admission limits should not invalidate supported persisted data or alter previously recorded amounts.

by_item.statement: An expense beyond the service's exact representation capacity leaves the committed state intact.

why.opus: Accepting integers beyond exact representation would make balances wrong; rejecting them cleanly without using up a number is careful engineering.
why.grok: Accepting a cent amount that cannot be represented exactly would corrupt balances, so it should be rejected without consuming an expense number.
why.sol: Representation overflow must not corrupt committed amounts or consume an unsuccessful expense's number.

by_item.statement: An assignment body must give one unambiguous ownership instruction

why.opus: Rejecting duplicate JSON keys needs a custom parser beyond the request; taking the last value is standard JSON.parse behaviour.
why.grok: The API forbids unknown fields but is silent on duplicate keys, so last-key-wins and a 400 are both compatible.
why.sol: Rejecting duplicate JSON members rather than applying a consistent parser policy is unspecified.

by_item.statement: A data file with malformed UTF-8 in a saved assignee is refused at startup

why.opus: Byte-level UTF-8 validation of an externally corrupted data file is hardening beyond the request.
why.grok: An assignee containing invalid UTF-8 would load as the wrong owner, so startup should refuse that file.
why.sol: Silently replacing invalid bytes could load a different assignee from the one stored.

by_item.statement: An assignee cannot introduce a line break into a raw CLI record

why.opus: Escaping Unicode line separators for readers that treat them as line breaks goes beyond the LF-delimited raw format.
why.grok: The documented raw listing is LF-delimited, so also forcing Unicode line-break readers to see one record is an extra output encoding.
why.sol: Accepted assignee names should not corrupt the existing raw listing's record boundaries.

by_item.statement: An assignment body with malformed UTF-8 is rejected

why.opus: Rejecting malformed UTF-8 or decoding it with replacement characters are both defensible when the request is silent.
why.grok: A body that is not JSON is a documented 400 invalid, and a rejected request does not change the ticket, audit, or outbox.
why.sol: Malformed encoding must not silently turn the requested assignee into a different name.

by_item.statement: An operator can trace a notice to the exact assignment that queued it

why.opus: Tracing each notice to its exact audit entry through the notice key is added scope.
why.grok: The agent must be notified, but the notice key is not required to join each delivery to a distinct audit actor.
why.sol: Exact notice-to-audit correlation is an optional key design beyond the documented notification guarantees.

by_item.statement: Using a symbolic link as DATA_FILE cannot silently split an existing store into two copies.

why.opus: Handling a symlinked DATA_FILE is deployment hardening beyond the request.
why.grok: Keeping a symlink and its target as one store is filesystem-edge scope the requested JSON file does not mention.
why.sol: Accepting a linked store and silently separating it from its backing file risks apparent data loss.

by_item.statement: A stale special-move field leaves the rest of the position usable.

why.opus: Stale castling or en-passant fields make the FEN inconsistent; accepting it while ignoring them, or rejecting it, are both correct.
why.grok: Castling still needs a rook on the home square and en passant still needs a capturable pawn, while ordinary king and pawn moves remain legal.
why.sol: The request does not require tolerating stale special-move metadata instead of rejecting the position.

by_item.statement: Retargeting a state link during service leaves both snapshots intact

why.opus: Retargeting a state symlink while the service runs is hardening beyond the request.
why.grok: Retargeting the state symlink mid-request and keeping both snapshots byte-identical is not part of the documented save.
why.sol: Refusing retargeting with HTTP 500 is one of several possible safe path-handling policies.

by_item.statement: Agent names cannot contain Unicode line breaks

why.opus: Rejecting these characters narrows the agent name the request defines: any non-empty name of at most 64 characters.
why.grok: The request allows any non-empty agent name of at most 64 characters, and these separators do not break the documented LF record format.
why.sol: Rejecting line separators is one policy; accepting them with safe output encoding is another.

by_item.statement: CLI assignment history distinguishes a cleared assignee from any agent name

why.opus: How the CLI shows unassigned next to names like '—' or 'null' is a display choice.
why.grok: The request asks the listing to show the assignee, not for show to render history that distinguishes an em dash, the name null, and a clear.
why.sol: Displaying an unassigned value indistinguishably from a valid agent name makes history misleading.

by_item.statement: Malformed UTF-8 cannot stand for an agent name

why.opus: Rejecting or replacing malformed UTF-8 in bodies and queries are both defensible when the request is silent.
why.grok: A raw 0xFF is not an agent name or a valid filter, while a real U+FFFD character is a legal name and must still round-trip.
why.sol: Malformed encoding must not alias a different, correctly encoded agent name.

by_item.statement: Assignment saves through a state-file symlink keep the linked snapshot current

why.opus: Supporting a symlinked DATA_FILE through the existing temp-file-and-rename save is outside the assignment change.
why.grok: The documented save is a temp file and rename; special symlink preservation or startup refusal is not part of adding assignment.
why.sol: An accepted state-file symlink should not silently separate persisted assignments from its backing snapshot.

by_item.statement: The API documents how to address accepted IDs that a URL client would normalize.

why.opus: Documenting how to address the IDs '.' and '..' is extra documentation scope.
why.grok: The request neither asks for API documentation nor requires . or .. to be accepted as group ids.
why.sol: The request does not prescribe documentation for client-specific handling of unusual accepted IDs.

by_item.statement: A query string does not change the operation or the addressed group.

why.opus: The request is silent on query strings; ignoring them or rejecting the URL are both acceptable.
why.grok: The routes are specified without query strings, so ignoring a query and rejecting it are both compatible with the API.
why.sol: Ignoring unspecified query parameters is a policy choice; rejecting them could also be correct.

by_item.statement: An operator hands over a store created after an earlier process started

why.opus: Handing store ownership between processes goes well beyond the request.
why.grok: Starting before the data directory exists and later adopting another process's store is not part of the requested persistence.
why.sol: Delayed store acquisition and live ownership handover add an operational lifecycle absent from the request.

by_item.statement: A failed title save leaves the committed title available for assignment notices

why.opus: A failed save must not leave an uncommitted title that a later assignment notice or save would use.
why.grok: A failed title save leaves the committed ticket, so a later assignment and its notice can only use that committed title.
why.sol: The documented atomic change requires a failed title save to preserve the committed ticket and audit.

by_item.statement: A malformed percent escape cannot select an agent with a literal percent sign

why.opus: Rejecting a bare '%' or decoding it leniently are both acceptable.
why.grok: The assignee filter has to percent-decode Dana%25 to find Dana%, and a dangling % must not select that agent.
why.sol: Strict rejection of malformed percent escapes is an unspecified query-decoding policy.

by_item.statement: The API documents the HTTP size budget separately from the group ID limit.

why.opus: Documenting an HTTP size budget is not asked for.
why.grok: The request does not define an HTTP header or request-target budget, or require that budget to be documented.
why.sol: A documented combined HTTP size budget is an optional admission-policy detail.

by_item.statement: The first successful move clears unsupported castling flags for either color in the returned FEN.

why.opus: Clearing unsupported flags in the output is one way to handle bad input; keeping them or rejecting the FEN is also defensible.
why.grok: On an inconsistent position, an unrelated pawn move may keep stale castling flags or clear flags whose king or rook is already off home.
why.sol: Immediately normalizing unsupported castling flags is one possible policy for inconsistent input.

by_item.statement: En-passant eligibility is independent of the move counters.

why.opus: En-passant legality does not depend on the counters, and the request requires a pawn capture to reset the halfmove clock.
why.grok: The request makes the en-passant square authoritative and the halfmove clock a separate field that a capture resets to zero.
why.sol: The request does not specify accepting an en-passant field inconsistent with the halfmove clock.

by_item.statement: Splitting a UTF-8 character across upload chunks preserves the assignee

why.opus: Decoding each body chunk separately would corrupt a multibyte character in the name.
why.grok: The stored assignee is the JSON string, so splitting a UTF-8 character across body chunks must not change the name, filter, or recipient.
why.sol: Transport chunk boundaries cannot change a valid assignment name or its notification recipient.

by_item.statement: The position APIs accept equivalent FEN field formatting.

why.opus: Accepting tabs, leading zeros and reordered castling letters goes beyond the standard FEN the request names.
why.grok: The request asks for FEN positions, not for tabs, extra spaces, reordered castling letters, or leading zeroes to be accepted.
why.sol: Tolerance for noncanonical whitespace, castling order and numeric formatting is unspecified.

by_item.statement: A resolvable state symlink can select a new snapshot

why.opus: Creating a new snapshot through a symlink to a missing file is beyond scope.
why.grok: Creating a missing snapshot through a dangling symlink and keeping that symlink is not the documented file behavior.
why.sol: Supporting a dangling state symlink is optional; a correct implementation could refuse that configuration.

by_item.statement: The service reports a path conflict between the state file and notification sink

why.opus: Detecting that DATA_FILE and NOTIFY_FILE are the same path is configuration hardening the request does not ask for.
why.grok: Diagnosing DATA_FILE and NOTIFY_FILE when they are the same path is pre-existing configuration hardening, not part of assignment.
why.sol: Conflicting state and notification destinations must not silently corrupt the store.

by_item.statement: The human-readable CLI distinguishes names containing text direction overrides

why.opus: Neutralising bidirectional-override characters in CLI output is beyond scope.
why.grok: The listing must show the assignee, but isolating bidirectional overrides so a name cannot visually reorder fields is a display choice.
why.sol: Direction controls can otherwise misrepresent an owner and reorder surrounding displayed ticket information.

by_item.statement: The service documents and enforces its group ID size limit in percent-encoded bytes.

why.opus: A documented 48 KiB limit on group IDs in percent-encoded bytes is invented scope.
why.grok: The request does not impose a group-id length limit or define it in percent-encoded bytes.
why.sol: Neither an ID size limit nor measuring it in percent-encoded bytes is specified.

by_item.statement: The service documents any fixed per-expense amount limit and applies it to new inputs.

why.opus: Documenting a fixed limit on expense length is not asked for.
why.grok: The request does not impose a fixed decimal length for new amounts or require that limit to be documented.
why.sol: A fixed decimal-length admission limit and its documentation are implementation choices.

by_item.statement: A hard-linked DATA_FILE cannot silently split an existing store into separate snapshots.

why.opus: Handling a hard-linked data file is hardening beyond the request.
why.grok: Preserving hard-link identity of the data file is outside the requested single-file store.
why.sol: Silently splitting an accepted store's aliases can make acknowledged expenses disappear through another existing path.

by_item.statement: An assignment notice retains the ticket title from the time of assignment

why.opus: A notice could use the title at assignment time or at delivery; both are defensible.
why.grok: The outbox stores a notification's payload when it is queued, so a later rename must not change that assignment's title.
why.sol: The request neither requires titles in assignment notices nor selects assignment-time versus delivery-time titles.

by_item.statement: Opening a legacy data file for service reads leaves it untouched

why.opus: Rewriting a legacy file on load or leaving it untouched until the first change are both acceptable.
why.grok: The data file is loaded at start and rewritten only after a change, so reading a pre-assignment file must leave its bytes untouched.
why.sol: A safe eager migration could rewrite a legacy snapshot while preserving all required behavior.

by_item.statement: A running service cannot silently overwrite a changed store with stale data.

why.opus: Detecting an outside replacement of the data file while the service runs goes beyond the request.
why.grok: The service owns in-memory state and rewrites its file; detecting an outside replacement, even one that forges file identity, is extra.
why.sol: Detecting conflicting store changes prevents a stale process from silently destroying replacement data.

by_item.statement: Corrupt saved assignment names are refused before serving or delivery

why.opus: Byte-level UTF-8 checks on corrupted saved names are hardening beyond the request.
why.grok: An invalid UTF-8 byte in a saved assignee or pending recipient would corrupt that name, while a real U+FFFD must still load.
why.sol: Malformed encoding must not silently change saved ownership or notification recipients.

by_item.statement: CLI history distinguishes an unassignment from assignment to a literal name

why.opus: How CLI history shows unassignment against a literal 'null' name is a display choice.
why.grok: Distinguishing a clear from an agent whose name is null in show's history is not requested; the listing only has to show the assignee.
why.sol: An unassignment and assignment to the literal name null must not produce misleadingly identical history.

by_item.statement: An operator restarts after an interrupted snapshot save

why.opus: A crash during a save must not corrupt or lose the persisted data that the request says survives a restart.
why.grok: A crash during a save must leave the last committed groups and the next expense number intact, or a restart loses data.
why.sol: An interrupted save must not destroy previously committed data or make abandoned candidates authoritative.

by_item.statement: Each contiguous run of empty squares in a FEN rank uses a single digit.

why.opus: Rejecting non-canonical digit runs such as '44' and accepting them are both reasonable parser behaviours.
why.grok: The request never says how syntactically invalid FEN is handled, so throwing on a rank written as 44 is optional.
why.sol: The request defines FEN inputs but does not prescribe rejection behavior for malformed FEN.

by_item.statement: The documented HTTP size budget tells clients how to stay within its usable boundary.

why.opus: Documenting how clients size requests near the limit is not asked for.
why.grok: The request does not ask for documentation of how clients should size requests against an HTTP byte limit.
why.sol: The request does not require a documented transport-budget calculation or select its boundary convention.

by_item.statement: An en-passant target is unusable if the double push would have left the pushing side's king in check.

why.opus: Checking whether the earlier double push was legal is retrograde analysis the request does not ask for.
why.grok: The request treats the FEN en-passant square as the eligibility signal and does not add a retrograde test that the implied double push was legal.
why.sol: Historical validation of en-passant metadata in an already inconsistent position is unspecified.

by_item.statement: Raw CLI consumers can identify record boundaries when titles contain Unicode line separators

why.opus: It concerns existing titles and CLI documentation, not the assignment change.
why.grok: Documenting LF versus Unicode line separators inside existing titles is outside the assignment request.
why.sol: This adds Unicode-separator title support and a raw-format documentation contract outside the assignment request.

by_item.statement: Malformed UTF-8 is rejected before it can change stored identifiers.

why.opus: Strictly validating UTF-8 in bodies and in snapshots is hardening the request does not ask for.
why.grok: Malformed UTF-8 is not valid JSON and must not be allowed to change stored ids or be rewritten into the snapshot.
why.sol: Replacing malformed UTF-8 silently can change identifiers and corrupt persisted meaning.

by_item.statement: The raw CLI documents how consumers recover the exact assignee

why.opus: A documented escaping and decoding rule for the raw fifth field is added scope.
why.grok: The raw listing must show the assignee without moving the old columns, but a documented reversible escape encoding is only one way to do that.
why.sol: Ambiguous escaping would make raw consumers recover the wrong assignee.

by_item.statement: A client reconnects after losing an expense response

why.opus: Committed expenses must persist, and every POST records a new expense with the next number.
why.grok: A committed expense must survive restart, and another POST is a new expense because the request defines no idempotency key.
why.sol: Committed expenses must survive restart, and another valid POST records another expense without an idempotency contract.

by_item.statement: Successful JSON results identify their HTTP media type.

why.opus: A JSON API without an application/json Content-Type can be misread by clients.
why.grok: The request specifies the status codes and JSON bodies, not a Content-Type header.
why.sol: JSON responses should identify their representation so HTTP clients can interpret them correctly.

by_item.statement: An assignee filter with malformed UTF-8 is rejected

why.opus: Rejecting a malformed UTF-8 query value or decoding it leniently are both defensible.
why.grok: A filter must select the real U+FFFD name when it is percent-encoded, and %FF is malformed UTF-8 so it is a 400.
why.sol: Malformed UTF-8 must not select an agent whose actual name contains a replacement character.

by_item.statement: Every reader diagnoses malformed UTF-8 anywhere in a saved snapshot

why.opus: Requiring every reader to diagnose malformed UTF-8 anywhere in the file goes beyond the assignment change.
why.grok: Invalid UTF-8 anywhere in the snapshot would make every reader show bad data, so startup, the CLI, and the weekly report should refuse it and keep the bytes.
why.sol: All readers should reject corrupt encoding rather than silently report altered snapshot data.

by_item.statement: An operator adopts a replacement snapshot after a stale-write refusal

why.opus: It builds on stale-write detection, which is already excess.
why.grok: Adopting an externally swapped snapshot after a stale-write refusal is an operator procedure the request never describes.
why.sol: Startup must load the configured valid snapshot and continue its saved expenses and numbering.
